messages:
maria: hey folks — onboarding sampleapp is getting hammered by 429s during the initial import. we prefetch 4 pages in parallel per user, and auth refresh sometimes retries a request which doubles the burst. any quick mitigations? :grimacing:

jen: ugh. are those 429s from our hosted API or the customer's rate limits? can you paste the request logs? :eyes:

maria: hosted. logs show a lot of overlapping calls for page cursors C1..C4. pattern: token-expiry triggers a refresh call that retries the original page fetch; the original also still proceeds -> double. sample trace: 
```
Request A -> 401 -> refresh token -> retry A
Request B -> normal 200
Request C -> 401 -> refresh token -> retry C
(while A retry still inflight) -> rapid 429s
```

sam: hmm that sounds like an auth-retry race + aggressive prefetch. quick fixes: 1) serialize auth-refresh per user (single-flight), 2) cap parallel prefetch per session to 2, 3) honor Retry-After header on 429s before retrying.

tao: exactly. for the SDK we already have a single-flight token refresh helper but sampleapp wasn't using it — it used naive fetch+if401->refresh->retry. considered adding an auth mutex or using the SDK's getAccessToken({forceRefresh:false}) helper?

maria: not using helper, yeah. curious if we should change sampleapp to adopt a semaphore around prefetch too. current code: `const prefetch = pages.map(p => fetchPage(p))` — all kicked off at once.

sam: switch to something like: 
```js
// pseudo
const limiter = new Semaphore(2);
await Promise.all(pages.map(p => limiter.acquire().then(async (release) => { try { return await fetchPage(p) } finally { release() } })))
```
That plus single-flight refresh should cut the burst ~3-4x.

jen: also add exponential backoff + jitter on retries and a cap of 3 attempts. And if you see 429s from a specific route, route to a lower-concurrency variant (we do route-level throttles in prod).

maria: nice. one more nuance: prefetch was doing cursor stitching — it would prefetch page N+1 before N resolved. maybe change to prefetch only after the parent page resolves or keep at most one ahead.

tao: good call. we can update sampleapp to: prefetchAhead = Math.min(1, platformConcurrencySuggested) and plug in SDK.getConcurrencyHint() later.

maria: i'll prototype changes: use single-flight refresh, limiter=2, prefetchAhead=1, backoff. i'll run with a small cohort behind feature flag. thanks y'all :heart:

ci-deploy-bot: Deploy queued: sampleapp/onboard-prefetch-fix -> staging (job #8245).

sam: once you have a repro, i can add a unit test for the refresh mutex and an integration test emulating simultaneous pages.

maria: will do. logging note: added a debug tag `dx.prefetch.concurrency` to correlate bursts.

jen: FYI, docs link: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/concurrency has examples for semaphores and single-flight auth helpers. also add a short blurb in onboarding quickstart about "avoid aggressive parallel prefetch on first-run".

maria: ack. filing a tiny PR now. ping me if you want to review the mutex pattern. :wave:
